name: Low Oxygen Affinity Beta Chain Hemoglobin Disease

criteria.description: Identification of hemoglobin variant with decreased oxygen affinity by hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Positive family history of hemoglobinopathy with similar oxygen affinity abnormalities
Clinical signs consistent with mild chronic tissue hypoxia such as mild erythrocytosis or cyanosis
Normal or slightly decreased oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry despite symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a low oxygen affinity beta chain hemoglobin variant confirmed by laboratory testing plus clinical evidence of mild chronic hypoxia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on specialized hemoglobin analysis and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mild cyanosis due to decreased oxygen saturation
pathognomonic.notes: Persistent mild cyanosis without cardiopulmonary disease
searchTerms: mild blue skin from low oxygen
slight cyanosis due to low saturation

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated red blood cell count as a compensatory response
searchTerms: slight excess of red blood cells

common.notes: Shortness of breath on physical activity

common.symptomName: Mild fatigue related to tissue hypoxia
searchTerms: low energy due to poor oxygen delivery

common.notes: Intermittent headaches possibly related to oxygen delivery
searchTerms: head pain from low oxygen levels

common.notes: Increased heart rate as compensatory mechanism

occasional.notes: Enlarged spleen due to increased red cell turnover

searchTerms: getting tired easily with physical activity

rare.notes: Rare cerebrovascular events possibly due to altered oxygen delivery
Rare thrombotic events secondary to erythrocytosis

laboratory: Hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC showing beta chain variant with decreased oxygen affinity
Mild erythrocytosis on complete blood count
Normal or slightly decreased oxygen saturation on arterial blood gas
imaging: Usually normal chest X-ray and echocardiogram
Occasional mild splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
other: Pulse oximetry may show mild desaturation not explained by cardiopulmonary disease

distinguishingFeatures: Increased oxygen affinity causing tissue hypoxia with compensatory erythrocytosis
Presence of methemoglobin on blood analysis

redFlags: Severe hypoxia unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of thrombotic complications such as stroke or deep vein thrombosis
